references.citation: Association of Anaesthetists. Quick Reference Handbook: 3-10 Local anaesthetic toxicity, version 2. June 2023. The Association states this QRH page, not the withdrawn 2010 laminate, is the current UK reference version.
references.excerpt: If circulatory arrest: start continuous CPR using standard protocols but give intravenous lipid emulsion; use a smaller adrenaline dose (<= 1 microgram/kg instead of 1 mg); avoid vasopressin. Box A: give an initial i.v. bolus of lipid emulsion 1.5 ml/kg over 2-3 min (~100 ml for a 70 kg adult); start an i.v. infusion at 15 ml/kg/h; at 5 and 10 minutes give a repeat bolus if cardiovascular stability has not been restored; at any time after 5 minutes double the rate to 30 ml/kg/h if the circulation is not restored; do not exceed maximum cumulative dose 12 ml/kg (70 kg: 840 ml). Use 20% Intralipid; propofol is not a suitable substitute.

cards.question: How should local-anaesthetic dose limits be selected?
cards.answer: Use the exact product, route and procedure table, not a universal maximum-safe dose. Named UK lidocaine 2% (emc 15150) limits a single dose to 4.5 mg/kg and 300 mg; more conservative local policies may apply. Xylocaine with adrenaline (emc 2397) has an adult single-dose ceiling 500 mg. Named bupivacaine field-block/infiltration (emc 11611) limits 150 mg; levobupivacaine (emc 13644) has single-dose 150 mg and daily 400 mg limits. These scopes are not interchangeable with spinal, major nerve blocks or IVRA; no universal ropivacaine/prilocaine maximum is inferred. Prior doses, mixed agents, vascularity, body-weight basis and patient factors matter. Below a listed ceiling, toxicity remains possible.

cards.question: How does pKa of a local anaesthetic relate to onset of action?
cards.answer: Only the unionised form crosses the nerve membrane. The closer the pKa to physiological pH, the higher the proportion unionised, and the faster the onset. Lidocaine pKa 7.9 — ~25 % unionised → onset 2–5 min. Bupivacaine pKa 8.1 — ~15 % unionised → onset 10–15 min. In infected tissue (low pH), more drug is ionised → poor onset (textbook reason to avoid LA in abscesses). Chloroprocaine (pKa 8.7) is exception — fastest onset due to high concentration used.

cards.question: Outline the management of local-anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST).
cards.answer: Association of Anaesthetists QRH 3-10 (2023) algorithm: STOP injection, call for help, ABC (100 % O₂, secure airway, IV access). Manage seizures with a small incremental benzodiazepine dose (thiopental or propofol only with caution because of negative inotropy). If arrest, give adrenaline ≤ 1 microgram/kg, avoid vasopressin and lidocaine, and use amiodarone for ventricular arrhythmias. Give 20 % lipid emulsion 1.5 mL/kg over 2–3 min, then 15 mL/kg/h; repeat the bolus at 5 and 10 min and double to 30 mL/kg/h if unstable; maximum cumulative 12 mL/kg. Continue CPR — long resuscitation is often successful. Refer to critical care and report the incident locally and nationally.
